log_log_richness_vs_library.interpretation: Sub-linear positive scaling: a 10x larger library yields only about 1.18x more observed features, consistent with sampling from a large unobserved pool rather than with exhaustive enumeration.

taylor_across_samples_closed.reason: Every row of the closed matrix sums to 1, so the across-feature mean is exactly 1/n_features for every sample: the x-axis of the Taylor relation is constant by construction and no slope is estimable.

closure_effect_on_taylor: Closing the rows destroys the across-feature Taylor relation by construction: the per-sample mean is pinned to 1/n_features, so the mean-variance slope is not estimable on the closed scale. Scale behaviour must therefore be assessed on the raw counts, and any per-feature comparison must condition on library size.
rarefaction_interpretation: Rarefied richness rises steeply with sequencing depth and never saturates, so raw richness is a depth-dependent statistic. At the smallest common depth (1000 counts, well below every sample's observed library) only about 31 of the mean 156 raw features are still visible: the composition is dominated by entities that the sampled depth does not reach.
pairwise_logratio_interpretation: Median pairwise log-ratio variance across the full sample set is about 4.09, far above the < 1 range that would indicate near-proportional (stable-ratio) behaviour, and it is dominated by which samples contain both members at all (median joint presence 0.130).
clr_pca_interpretation: No low-dimensional invariant dominates: the leading CLR axis carries only 21.9% of variance and 50% of variance needs 7 axes. The spectrum is also stable under pseudocount choice, so this is a property of the data and not of the zero-replacement rule.

occupancy_abundance.interpretation: Prevalence and abundance are strongly and monotonically coupled, which is the classic signature of a shared underlying abundance distribution sampled at limited depth.
